title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Price increase (4.5%)
drivers.evidence: Past price hikes of 20%+ show median 13% lift in price, but demand drops 10–15% on average; noise-adjusted estimate for 4.5% increase is x0.87.

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: Monday closure reduces potential sales by ~14% for a 7-day week; no evidence of full-week substitution, but demand is non-essential.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 96.5. The target week has a 4.5% price increase to $10.32 (above regular $9.88) and a store closure on Monday. Price increases typically reduce demand; past 20%+ price hikes show median x0.85–0.90 vs baseline. A store closure on Monday (1/7 of the week) reduces potential sales by ~14%, but the product is non-essential and demand may be partially shifted. No promotion or event is scheduled. The classical uplift model suggests no effect, but this ignores price and closure. Evidence for price impact is moderate (2 past price increases, noise-adjusted x0.87). Closure effect is uncertain but plausible. Combined, a downward adjustment is warranted, shrunk toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-15 (5 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.32 (+4.5% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.5 | 5%-95%: 62.6 - 233.8 | 10%-90%: 67.2 - 191.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
